title: What Is Salvation?
content: Salvation in Christianity means deliverance from sin and its consequences through faith in Jesus Christ. It includes forgiveness of sins, reconciliation with God, and the gift of eternal life. Salvation is a work of God's grace received by faith.

title: Repentance and Faith
content: Repentance means turning away from sin and turning toward God. Faith is trusting in Jesus Christ as Lord and Savior. Genuine repentance and faith go together as responses to the Gospel.

title: Justification
content: Justification is God's declaration that a sinner is righteous based on the finished work of Christ. It is not earned by works but granted through faith. Christ's righteousness is credited to believers.

title: Regeneration
content: Regeneration is the spiritual new birth brought about by the Holy Spirit. It transforms the heart and gives new spiritual life. Jesus described this as being 'born again.'

title: Sanctification
content: Sanctification is the ongoing process by which believers grow in holiness and Christlikeness. It begins at salvation and continues throughout the Christian life through the work of the Holy Spirit.

title: Glorification
content: Glorification is the final stage of salvation when believers are fully transformed and receive resurrected bodies. It will occur at Christ's return and marks the completion of redemption.
